scenes.narration: One setting decides if AI plays safe or gets wild.
Welcome to FredsDesk, lesson ten. In under a minute, you'll learn what temperature does.
Temperature is a setting that controls how adventurous a model is when it picks its next word.
scenes.definition: Low means safe, predictable picks. High means varied, surprising picks.

scenes.narration: Think of ordering at a restaurant. A low-temperature diner always picks the favorite dish. A high-temperature diner is happy to try anything on the menu.
Take the sentence, the sky is. The model scores each next word: blue, clear, gray, or purple. Low temperature almost always takes the top score. High temperature gives the others a real chance.
scenes.footer: Illustrative scores for the next word

scenes.narration: Same prompt, different settings. A low setting gives a safe slogan. A high one gives a wilder slogan.

messages.text: High: Sunshine in a cup, squeezed just for you!

scenes.narration: Quick recap. One: temperature controls how adventurous the picks are. Two: low is predictable. Three: high is creative, but riskier.
Quiz time! For a wild poem, which is better: A, high temperature, or B, low temperature? Answer in the comments. Tomorrow: what is training data? Follow FredsDesk, and see you at the desk.
